title: Engine Controls — Thrust Lever Detent Use and Manual Thrust Limitations
abstract: Flight crew limitation on the use of the thrust lever detents and on manual thrust setting, including what to do when a detent cannot be felt reliably.

sections.purpose: This entry states the limitations that apply to the use of the thrust lever detents and to manual thrust setting when the autothrust is not engaged.
sections.description: Thrust is set by placing the levers in a detent, and the detent is what tells the crew where the lever is without looking at it. Each detent has a defined tactile step, and the aircraft interprets the lever position rather than the force applied, so a lever left between detents commands something other than what the crew intends. On high-hour aircraft the detent can become soft, and crews report that the step at the climb gate is difficult or impossible to feel. A soft detent is not a control failure and the lever position is still interpreted correctly, but it removes the tactile confirmation the procedure relies on and it must be reported. When the detent cannot be felt, the lever position must be confirmed visually against the gate marking before the thrust setting is accepted.
sections.crew_procedure: Place the levers positively in the detent and confirm the position against the gate marking whenever the tactile step is not clear. Do not set thrust by matching a parameter with the levers between detents. Report a soft or absent detent with the gate concerned.
sections.limitation_note: Manual thrust setting with the levers between detents is not permitted. Where a detent cannot be felt, the lever position must be confirmed visually against the gate marking before the setting is accepted.

type_data.crew_action: Place the levers positively in the detent and confirm visually where the tactile step is not clear.

issue.reason: The visual confirmation of lever position is recorded as the approved interim mitigation for a soft detent, and the reporting is refined to name the direction in which the step was lost.

sections.purpose: This entry states the limitations that apply to the use of the thrust lever detents and to manual thrust setting when the autothrust is not engaged.
sections.description: Thrust is set by placing the levers in a detent, and the detent is what tells the crew where the lever is without looking at it. Each detent has a defined tactile step, and the aircraft interprets the lever position rather than the force applied, so a lever left between detents commands something other than what the crew intends. On high-hour aircraft the detent can become soft, and crews report that the step at the climb gate is difficult or impossible to feel. A soft detent is not a control failure and the lever position is still interpreted correctly, but it removes the tactile confirmation the procedure relies on and it must be reported. When the detent cannot be felt, the lever position must be confirmed visually against the gate marking before the thrust setting is accepted.
sections.crew_procedure: Place the levers positively in the detent and confirm the position against the gate marking whenever the tactile step is not clear. Do not set thrust by matching a parameter with the levers between detents. Report a soft or absent detent with the gate concerned and whether it was felt in one direction only, because that distinction is what the maintenance measurement looks for.
sections.limitation_note: Manual thrust setting with the levers between detents is not permitted. Where a detent cannot be felt, the lever position must be confirmed visually against the gate marking before the setting is accepted. That visual confirmation is the accepted interim mitigation for a soft detent and is what allows an aircraft to keep flying while it waits in the quadrant exchange queue; it is not a workaround adopted locally by crews but a published limitation, and it is quoted as such in the operator communication. A detent reported as absent must be measured before the next revenue sector where the operator's procedure requires it.
